title: Responses compatibility prober and graceful degradation scenarios
creator: Maya Fernandez
description: Objective: build a lightweight compatibility prober and a set of graceful-degradation scenarios that automatically detect feature gaps between Redwood's Responses-compatible runtime and upstream OpenAI Responses semantics. This ticket defines the probes, the observable signals we will collect, the heuristic scoring for incompatibilities, and the set of runtime fallback behaviors.
deliverables: 1) Compatibility prober harness (synthetic and recorded traffic) that exercises streaming events, function/tool calling edge behaviors, structured-output contracts, and error conditions. 2) Heuristic gap-scoring algorithm and a small dashboard summarizing per-model/per-feature drift. 3) A documented runbook of graceful-degradation scenarios (fallback models, event coalescing, trimmed structured outputs) and automated rollout gates tied to the prober score.
approach: Phase A: Define the feature matrix and probe cases. Phase B: Implement probes in the test-harness (unit, integration, and fuzz). Phase C: Ship a low-cost telemetry pipeline to capture event diffs and gap scores. Phase D: Implement fallback policies in routing layer and smoke canaries. We will prioritize determinism and reproducibility: every probe run should produce a diff artifact stored with timestamps.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prober can run a full feature matrix against a given model and produce a gap report within 30 minutes.
- Gap-scoring returns stable categories: behavioral, event-ordering, toolcall-schema, streaming-truncation.
- For any gap score above threshold, the routing policy can automatically divert traffic to a compatible variant and tag requests for manual review.
- Documentation and runbook with concrete mitigation steps exists and has been reviewed by runtime and SDK owners.
- Telemetry events are ingested into the dev console dashboard and are queryable by date/model/feature.
